prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / style-transfer.
Deliver ONE revised adult female archer illustration, actual transparent RGBA background.

Image roles:
IMAGE 1 = edit target, used ONLY to lock the body skeleton, low camera, perspective, crop, hands, bow and aiming action. Its HAIR, FACE, CLOTHES AND ARMOR have been explicitly rejected. Completely redraw those FOUR parts with the replacement designs below. Do not preserve the target's cosmetic identity or ornamental shapes.
IMAGE 2 = approved FACE reference ONLY. Use its rounded cheek volumes, short softly rounded chin, natural understated brows and eyes, lightly drawn lips and warm hand-painted expression. Do not copy its smiling mouth, body pose, costume, hair or background.
IMAGE 3 = Sdorica / 万象物语 painting reference ONLY: broad coherent planes, selective drawing, softly shaped volume, curved armor surfaces and focused light. No copying its character, pose, white hair, lettering or small chibi.

FOUR REQUIRED VISIBLE REPLACEMENTS — paint these from scratch:
1) HAIR: Crimson hair gathered tightly into a high ponytail held by a small smooth gold clasp. The crown is a connected hair cap. The ponytail sweeps up and left in THREE connected broad, flattened, gently tapering masses sharing ONE direction; these masses merge along their lengths and separate only near the ends. Leave a few broad bangs framing the face. Reduce the overgrown cloud of coils. Absolutely no circular loops, corkscrew ringlets, separate tubular ribbon locks, dense hairline etching, flyaway filaments, fuzzy glowing edges or alternating reflective stripes. Hair should feel pliable and naturally combed, with a continuous satin-matte red body and a single broad light transition, not a plastic toy or shredded brush.
2) GARMENT CONSTRUCTION: A single tailored sleeveless deep-purple top, a single brown leather waist belt, and a short purple wrap skirt joined at that waist. The short skirt consists of ONE broad front overlap and ONE back panel, with rounded corners, ending on the upper thighs. They move with the hips and have visibly understandable attachments. The front overlap maintains normal non-explicit coverage at the low camera angle. Bare upper arms and exposed upper thighs, brown knee-high boots below. No leggings or shorts added across the exposed thighs. REMOVE all hanging sleeve scarves, separate abdominal straps, pointed hip pennants, floating side ribbons, long central loincloth, trailing cape fragments and detached cloth behind either leg. Use a few actual tension folds near waist/hip seams and large quiet purple surfaces elsewhere. Keep character design interest in the neckline, hem cut and one clasp, not multiplying fabric pieces.
3) FACE: Repaint to image 2's hand-drawn facial proportions in image 1's existing three-quarter head orientation. A young ADULT woman with cheek volume and a softly rounded short chin, moderate natural almond-shaped amber eyes, subtle upper lids, unplucked-looking brows, a visibly modeled natural nose and a matte understated mouth. Focused and composed while aiming. Remove the sharp V-shaped jaw, pointed chin, doll-sized glassy eyes, dramatically upturned eyeliner, tiny pinched nose, glossy pout and beauty-filter porcelain shading. Avoid hard contour makeup. Do not keep image 1's generic glamour face.
4) ARMOR: Completely replace the jagged armor silhouettes with smooth curved warm-gold light armor. Each shoulder has ONE rounded cap with a rolled edge; each forearm has ONE broad curved cuff; each shin has ONE smooth tapered convex plate with a rounded knee cup and rounded lower edge. Articulation occurs through visible leather at elbows and knees, not piles of pointed overlapping scales. All external armor corners are rounded. No spikes, thorns, fins, chevrons, spear points, feather-shaped plates, serrated rims or crown prongs anywhere on the character. Decoration is limited to shallow engraved curves inside a few plates and one small rounded chest clasp. Broad satin metal surfaces, a few controlled reflected edges; no hammered patchwork, triangular facets, cracks or glitter. Keep the purple-and-warm-gold palette rather than swapping the armor to silver.

LOCKED ACTION:
Preserve image 1's low ground-level upward camera and the skeleton's exact projected locations. The near thigh and shin drive directly toward the viewer into the lower-right foreground, with a large foreshortened front boot. The far leg folds low to the left and the smaller far boot sits under the pelvis. Keep depth overlaps, torso twist, head position and shooting direction. Keep draw fingers anchored at the cheek, extended bow arm, coherent bowstring and ONE straight nocked arrow. Do not flatten, spread the legs sideways, create a floating seated squat, or change to standing/jumping. Maintain plausible anatomical joints and a load-bearing relation to an implied ground even without drawing scenery.

PAINT AND LIGHT:
Sdorica-inspired hand-painted surfaces and selective natural linework, coherent rich local colors. Large joined shadow shapes follow each whole volume; the body is NOT divided into random little colored polygons. Deep purple cloth remains deep purple through soft volume turns. A broad warm upper-right/front light concentrates on face and crown; the torso and lower body are quieter. Mostly matte/satin surfaces carry a few bright metal reflections and a small localized luminous hair/shoulder accent. No glowing outline around the entire figure. No global desaturation, mottled paper filter, grunge or noise pasted over the subject.

One character only. Genuine transparent background, no environment, rocks, dust, atmospheric color wash, black background, baked checkerboard, typography, labels or comparison panels.
The new result must have visibly DIFFERENT hair construction, face design, garment pattern and rounded armor silhouettes from image 1, while its camera and skeletal action remain unchanged.
